detail.body:
## Summary

Adds an identity hyper-connections (iHC) variant of mHC behind a new `TransformerConfig` flag, `enable_identity_hyper_connections` (CLI: `--enable-identity-hyper-connections`; requires `--enable-hyper-connections`).

With the flag on, `HyperConnectionModule` fixes the residual mixing matrix `H_res` to the `n x n` identity instead of the Sinkhorn-projected manifold matrix:

- `mapping_proj` only produces `H_pre` and `H_post` (`2n` outputs instead of `n^2 + 2n`); `alpha_res` and the `H_res` part of `bias` are not created.
- The `H_res` projection and the Sinkhorn-Knopp step are skipped entirely; `compute_mappings` materializes a per-token identity `[s, b, n, n]` in the activation dtype.
- The downstream `H_res` / `H_post` / BDA path (`fused_h_res_h_post_bda`, native and fused `h_post_bda` kernels, mHC recompute, CUDA graph plumbing) is unchanged and consumes the identity as-is. Kernel-level shortcuts for the identity case are left for a follow-up.
- With `use_fused_mhc=True`, aggregate and `h_post_bda` stay fused; the projection takes the native path because the fused `proj_rms_compute_h` kernel assumes the mHC output layout.
- mHC and iHC checkpoints are not interchangeable (parameter shapes differ).

The resulting propagation is `x_{l+1} = x_l + H_post^T @ F(H_pre @ x_l)`.

One change outside the module: `TransformerLayerNode.detach` in the fine-grained EP-overlap schedule now records a gradient bridge only for tensors that require grad. It used to hand every detached tensor to `run_backward`, which raises for a tensor without `grad_fn`; the constant iHC `h_res` is exactly that, so `overlap_moe_expert_parallel_comm` would have crashed. For mHC every bridged tensor requires grad, so behaviour there is unchanged (verified below).

## Test plan

New tests:
- `tests/unit_tests/transformer/test_identity_hyper_connection.py`: config validation, parameter layout (`2n` rows, no `alpha_res`), identity `h_res` in fp32 / bf16, empty-sequence forward/backward, output equals `x_l + H_post^T (F + bias)` stream by stream, iHC matches mHC whose Sinkhorn output is forced to the identity (outputs and gradients), `_forward_with_checkpoint` matches `_forward_normal`, `use_fused_mhc=True` path, `HyperConnectionTransformerLayer` forward/backward with and without `recompute_modules=[mhc]`.
- `tests/unit_tests/a2a_overlap/test_mhc_schedule.py::test_identity_hyper_connections_schedule_matches_eager` (EP=4 alltoall overlap schedule vs eager, with and without mHC recompute), placed last in its class.
- `tests/unit_tests/models/test_hybrid_moe_model.py`: the new field is registered in `GOLDEN_CONFIG`.

Why the iHC tests run under `torch.compiler.set_stance("force_eager")`: the constant `h_res` would otherwise add `requires_grad=False` guard variants to the `torch.compile`'d mHC kernels that every mHC test in the bucket shares (`native_h_post_bda`, `native_h_aggregate`, ...). Several existing eager-vs-schedule / eager-vs-graph comparisons (`test_full_recompute_carries_the_mhc_bridge_gradient`, `test_gpu_mhc_split_replay_matches_eager`) are sensitive to the compile-cache history: they fail when the default recompile limit of 8 is crossed, or a cold compile happens, between their two arms. On an 8x H100 node, clean `dev` fails `test_gpu_mhc_split_replay_matches_eager[True-False-False]` in a process that only runs `test_hyper_connection_recompute.py` before it, so this is pre-existing order sensitivity rather than an iHC regression; the eager stance keeps the cache history seen by those tests identical to `dev`. (An earlier revision of this PR reset the dynamo caches in the iHC teardowns instead; that changed the history and made CI fail the graph-split test, which is how this was found.)

Run on EOS, 8x H100, CI image `mcore-ci-dev`, `run_ci_test.sh --platform h100 --environment dev` (same markers as `cicd-unit-tests-latest`):
- `transformer/test_identity_hyper_connection.py`: 12 passed
- `transformer/test_hyper_connection_recompute.py`: 51 passed
- `a2a_overlap/test_mhc_schedule.py`: 25 passed (clean `dev` baseline on the same node: 23 passed)
- `transformer/test_hyper_connection_recompute.py` + `test_identity_hyper_connection.py` + `test_transformer_layer.py` in one pytest process: 123 passed

`black` / `isort` / `ruff` / `pylint` / copyright check pass against `dev`.

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""
+Unit tests for identity hyper-connections (iHC).
+
+iHC keeps the mHC H_pre / H_post mappings but fixes the residual mixing matrix
+H_res to the identity: no H_res parameters are learned and the Sinkhorn-Knopp
+step is skipped, while the downstream H_res / H_post / BDA kernels are unchanged.
+With use_fused_mhc the projection still runs through the fused kernel, fed zero
+H_res rows.
+Numerical references use full FP32 matmul precision so identity mixing preserves
+the residual even on devices where TF32 is selected for the native batched matmul.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.random import (
+    MHCCheckpointManager,
+    model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed,
+)
+from megatron.core.transformer.hyper_connection import HyperConnectionModule
+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import TransformerConfig
+from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_layer import HyperConnectionTransformerLayer
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module", autouse=True)
+def _model_parallel():
+    """Initialize model parallelism once for this module.
+
+    Every initialize/destroy cycle leaves its NCCL process groups (and their watchdog
+    threads) behind for the lifetime of the pytest process, and the CI bucket already
+    runs ~1700 tests in one process. Sharing one TP=1/PP=1 initialization across this
+    file keeps its footprint at a single cycle; the tests only need the RNG tracker and
+    a default group.
+    """
+    Utils.initialize_model_parallel(1, 1)
+    yield
+    Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _reseed(_model_parallel):
+    model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _full_fp32_matmul():
+    """Match the precision assumed by the strict identity/reference assertions.
+
+    CI containers can enable TF32 by default. On GB200 the native H_res batched
+    matmul then rounds the residual even for an identity matrix, unlike the
+    elementwise reference. Restore the original setting for subsequent tests.
+    """
+    previous_precision = torch.get_float32_matmul_precision()
+    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("highest")
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(previous_precision)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _run_eagerly():
+    """Run every test here with torch.compile stanced to eager.
+
+    iHC's constant H_res carries requires_grad=False, so letting these tests compile
+    would add guard variants to the mHC kernels (native_h_post_bda, native_h_aggregate,
+    ...) that every mHC test in this process shares. Under torch's default recompile
+    limit of 8 those extra variants can push a later mHC eager-vs-graph comparison into
+    the compiled-to-eager fallback on one side only (seen in CI on
+    test_mhc_attention_graph_split). The eager stance leaves the shared compile caches
+    exactly as the mHC tests expect them; the compiled kernels themselves are covered by
+    the mHC tests.
+    """
+    with torch.compiler.set_stance("force_eager"):
+        yield
+
+
+def _make_config(identity, hidden_size=64, num_streams=4, **extra):
+    """Build a hyper-connection TransformerConfig; ``identity`` selects iHC over mHC."""
+    base = dict(
+        num_layers=2,
+        hidden_size=hidden_size,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        use_cpu_initialization=True,
+        enable_hyper_connections=True,
+        enable_identity_hyper_connections=identity,
+        num_residual_streams=num_streams,
+        mhc_sinkhorn_iterations=5,
+        mhc_init_gating_factor=0.01,
+        hidden_dropout=0.0,
+        attention_dropout=0.0,
+    )
+    base.update(extra)
+    return TransformerConfig(**base)
+
+
+def _identity_h_res(s, b, n, dtype):
+    return torch.eye(n, dtype=dtype, device="cuda").expand(s, b, n, n)
+
+
+class TestIdentityHyperConnectionConfig:
+    def test_requires_hyper_connections(self):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="enable_identity_hyper_connections requires"):
+            TransformerConfig(
+                num_layers=2,
+                hidden_size=64,
+                num_attention_heads=4,
+                enable_identity_hyper_connections=True,
+            )
+
+
+class TestIdentityHyperConnectionModule:
+    def _make_module(self, identity=True, hidden_size=64, num_streams=4, **extra):
+        config = _make_config(identity, hidden_size, num_streams, **extra)
+        module = HyperConnectionModule(config=config, layer_number=1)
+        module.cuda()
+        return module
+
+    def test_parameter_layout_drops_h_res(self):
+        n, C = 4, 64
+        ihc = self._make_module(identity=True, num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        assert ihc.identity_h_res
+        assert ihc.mapping_proj.weight.shape == (2 * n, n * C)
+        assert ihc.bias.shape == (2 * n,)
+        assert ihc.alpha_res is None
+        assert {name for name, _ in ihc.named_parameters()} == {
+            "mapping_proj.weight",
+            "alpha_pre",
+            "alpha_post",
+            "bias",
+        }
+        assert ihc._sinkhorn_op is None
+        assert ihc._proj_rms_compute_h_op is None
+
+        mhc = self._make_module(identity=False, num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        assert not mhc.identity_h_res
+        assert mhc.mapping_proj.weight.shape == (n * n + 2 * n, n * C)
+        assert mhc.bias.shape == (n * n + 2 * n,)
+        assert mhc.alpha_res is not None
+        assert mhc._sinkhorn_op is not None
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+    def test_compute_mappings_returns_identity_h_res(self, dtype):
+        s, b, n, C = 8, 2, 4, 64
+        module = self._make_module(num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        x = torch.randn(s, b, n * C, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+
+        h_pre, h_post, h_res = module.compute_mappings(x)
+
+        assert h_pre.shape == (s, b, n) and h_pre.dtype == dtype
+        assert h_post.shape == (s, b, n) and h_post.dtype == dtype
+        assert h_res.shape == (s, b, n, n) and h_res.dtype == dtype
+        assert h_res.is_contiguous()
+        assert not h_res.requires_grad
+        torch.testing.assert_close(h_res, _identity_h_res(s, b, n, dtype), atol=0.0, rtol=0.0)
+        # H_pre / H_post keep their mHC ranges: sigmoid (+eps) and 2 * sigmoid.
+        assert torch.all(h_pre > 0) and torch.all(h_pre <= 1 + 1e-3)
+        assert torch.all(h_post >= 0) and torch.all(h_post <= 2)
+
+    def test_forward_supports_empty_sequence(self):
+        module = self._make_module(num_streams=2, hidden_size=4)
+        hidden_states = torch.empty(0, 1, 8, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+
+        aggregated, h_res, h_post, residual = module(hidden_states)
+
+        assert aggregated.shape == (0, 1, 4)
+        assert h_res.shape == (0, 1, 2, 2)
+        assert h_post.shape == (0, 1, 2)
+        assert residual.shape == (0, 1, 8)
+        (aggregated.sum() + h_post.sum() + residual.sum()).backward()
+        assert hidden_states.grad is not None
+        assert module.mapping_proj.weight.grad is not None
+
+    def test_output_is_residual_plus_h_post_expansion(self):
+        """With H_res = I the layer output is x_l + H_post^T @ (F + bias), stream by stream."""
+        s, b, n, C = 8, 2, 4, 64
+        module = self._make_module(num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(s, b, n * C, device="cuda")
+        layer_output = torch.randn(s, b, C, device="cuda")
+        layer_bias = torch.randn(C, device="cuda")
+
+        _, h_res, h_post, residual = module(hidden_states)
+        output = module.fused_h_res_h_post_bda(
+            h_res,
+            residual,
+            h_post,
+            (layer_output, layer_bias),
+            dropout_prob=0.0,
+            training=True,
+            fused=False,
+        )
+
+        expected = hidden_states.view(s, b, n, C) + h_post.unsqueeze(-1) * (
+            layer_output + layer_bias
+        ).unsqueeze(2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output, expected.view(s, b, n * C))
+
+    def test_matches_mhc_with_identity_residual_mixing(self):
+        """iHC must reproduce mHC whose Sinkhorn output is forced to the identity."""
+        s, b, n, C = 8, 2, 4, 64
+        ihc = self._make_module(identity=True, num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        mhc = self._make_module(identity=False, num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        with torch.no_grad():
+            mhc.mapping_proj.weight[: 2 * n].copy_(ihc.mapping_proj.weight)
+            mhc.bias[: 2 * n].copy_(ihc.bias)
+            mhc.alpha_pre.copy_(ihc.alpha_pre)
+            mhc.alpha_post.copy_(ihc.alpha_post)
+
+        def identity_sinkhorn(logits, num_iterations, eps):
+            return torch.eye(n, dtype=logits.dtype, device=logits.device).expand_as(logits)
+
+        mhc._sinkhorn_op = identity_sinkhorn
+
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(s, b, n * C, device="cuda")
+        layer_output = torch.randn(s, b, C, device="cuda")
+        mix = torch.randn(s, b, C, device="cuda")
+
+        def run(module):
+            hs = hidden_states.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+            aggregated, h_res, h_post, residual = module(hs)
+            output = module.fused_h_res_h_post_bda(
+                h_res,
+                residual,
+                h_post,
+                (aggregated * mix + layer_output, None),
+                dropout_prob=0.0,
+                training=True,
+                fused=False,
+            )
+            output.sum().backward()
+            return output.detach(), hs.grad
+
+        out_ihc, grad_ihc = run(ihc)
+        out_mhc, grad_mhc = run(mhc)
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_ihc, out_mhc, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(grad_ihc, grad_mhc, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            ihc.mapping_proj.weight.grad,
+            mhc.mapping_proj.weight.grad[: 2 * n],
+            atol=1e-5,
+            rtol=1e-4,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(ihc.bias.grad, mhc.bias.grad[: 2 * n], atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(ihc.alpha_pre.grad, mhc.alpha_pre.grad, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(ihc.alpha_post.grad, mhc.alpha_post.grad, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)
+
+    def test_forward_with_checkpoint_matches_normal(self):
+        s, b, n, C = 8, 2, 4, 64
+        module = self._make_module(num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(s, b, n * C, device="cuda")
+        layer_output = torch.randn(s, b, C, device="cuda")
+
+        def run(manager):
+            module.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+            hs = hidden_states.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+            aggregated, h_res, h_post, residual = module(hs, mhc_recompute_manager=manager)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                h_res, _identity_h_res(s, b, n, hs.dtype), atol=0.0, rtol=0.0
+            )
+            output = module.fused_h_res_h_post_bda(
+                h_res,
+                residual,
+                h_post,
+                (aggregated + layer_output, None),
+                dropout_prob=0.0,
+                training=True,
+                fused=False,
+                manager=manager,
+            )
+            loss = output.sum()
+            if manager is not None:
+                manager.discard_all_outputs_and_register_unified_recompute(loss)
+            loss.backward()
+            return output.detach().clone(), hs.grad.clone(), module.mapping_proj.weight.grad.clone()
+
+        out_ref, grad_ref, wgrad_ref = run(None)
+        out_ckpt, grad_ckpt, wgrad_ckpt = run(MHCCheckpointManager())
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_ckpt, out_ref)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(grad_ckpt, grad_ref, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(wgrad_ckpt, wgrad_ref, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
+
+    def test_fused_mapping_params_pad_h_res_rows(self):
+        """The fused projection is fed the mHC layout: real rows first, zero H_res rows."""
+        n, C = 4, 64
+        ihc = self._make_module(identity=True, num_streams=n, hidden_size=C, use_fused_mhc=True)
+        weight, alpha_res, bias = ihc._fused_mapping_params()
+        assert weight.shape == (n * n + 2 * n, n * C)
+        assert bias.shape == (n * n + 2 * n,)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(weight[: 2 * n], ihc.mapping_proj.weight, atol=0.0, rtol=0.0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(bias[: 2 * n], ihc.bias, atol=0.0, rtol=0.0)
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(weight[2 * n :]) == 0
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(bias[2 * n :]) == 0
+        assert alpha_res.shape == (1,) and not alpha_res.requires_grad
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(alpha_res) == 0
+
+        mhc = self._make_module(identity=False, num_streams=n, hidden_size=C, use_fused_mhc=True)
+        weight, alpha_res, bias = mhc._fused_mapping_params()
+        assert weight is mhc.mapping_proj.weight
+        assert alpha_res is mhc.alpha_res
+        assert bias is mhc.bias
+
+    def test_use_fused_mhc_matches_native_projection(self):
+        """use_fused_mhc routes the iHC projection through the fused kernel, matching native."""
+        from megatron.core.fusions.fused_mhc_kernels import fused_proj_rms_compute_h
+
+        s, b, n, C = 8, 2, 4, 64
+        fused = self._make_module(num_streams=n, hidden_size=C, use_fused_mhc=True)
+        native = self._make_module(num_streams=n, hidden_size=C)
+        native.load_state_dict(fused.state_dict())
+        assert fused._proj_rms_compute_h_op is fused_proj_rms_compute_h
+        assert fused._sinkhorn_op is None
+        assert fused.alpha_res is None
+
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(s, b, n * C, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        layer_output = torch.randn(s, b, C, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+        def run(module):
+            module.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+            hs = hidden_states.clone().requires_grad_(True)
+            aggregated, h_res, h_post, residual = module(hs)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                h_res, _identity_h_res(s, b, n, torch.bfloat16), atol=0.0, rtol=0.0
+            )
+            output = module.fused_h_res_h_post_bda(
+                h_res,
+                residual,
+                h_post,
+                (aggregated + layer_output, None),
+                dropout_prob=0.0,
+                training=True,
+                fused=False,
+            )
+            output.float().sum().backward()
+            grads = {name: p.grad.clone() for name, p in module.named_parameters()}
+            return (
+                h_post.detach().float(),
+                aggregated.detach().float(),
+                output.detach().float(),
+                hs.grad.float(),
+                grads,
+            )
+
+        post_f, agg_f, out_f, gx_f, grads_f = run(fused)
+        post_n, agg_n, out_n, gx_n, grads_n = run(native)
+
+        # Same tolerances as the fused-kernel tests: the cuTile backend accumulates
+        # in mixed precision.
+        fwd_tol = dict(atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+        bwd_tol = dict(atol=5e-2, rtol=5e-2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(post_f, post_n, **fwd_tol)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(agg_f, agg_n, **fwd_tol)
+        # out = residual + h_post * F: a one-ulp bf16 difference in h_post (the cuTile
+        # projection uses TF32 MMAs, the reference here full FP32) is scaled by |F|, which
+        # reaches ~3 for these inputs, so the absolute tolerance must cover ~0.03.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out_f, out_n, atol=5e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(gx_f, gx_n, **bwd_tol)
+        assert grads_f.keys() == grads_n.keys()
+        assert set(grads_n) == {"mapping_proj.weight", "alpha_pre", "alpha_post", "bias"}
+        assert grads_f["mapping_proj.weight"].shape == (2 * n, n * C)
+        assert grads_f["bias"].shape == (2 * n,)
+        for name in grads_n:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(grads_f[name], grads_n[name], msg=name, **bwd_tol)
+
+
+class TestIdentityHyperConnectionTransformerLayer:
+    def _make_layer(self, hidden_size=64, num_streams=4, **extra):
+        config = _make_config(True, hidden_size, num_streams, **extra)
+        layer_spec = get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec(enable_hyper_connection=True)
+        layer = HyperConnectionTransformerLayer(config, layer_spec.submodules, layer_number=1)
+        layer.cuda()
+        layer.train()
+        return layer
+
+    def test_layer_builds_identity_hyper_connections(self):
+        layer = self._make_layer()
+        for module in (layer.self_attention_hyper_connection, layer.mlp_hyper_connection):
+            assert isinstance(module, HyperConnectionModule)
+            assert module.identity_h_res
+            assert module.alpha_res is None
+            assert module.mapping_proj.weight.shape[0] == 2 * layer.config.num_residual_streams
+
+    def test_forward_backward(self):
+        hidden_size, n, s, b = 64, 4, 8, 2
+        layer = self._make_layer(hidden_size=hidden_size, num_streams=n)
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(s, b, n * hidden_size, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+        attention_mask = torch.ones((1, 1, s, s), dtype=bool, device="cuda")
+
+        output, _ = layer(hidden_states=hidden_states, attention_mask=attention_mask)
+
+        assert output.shape == (s, b, n * hidden_size)
+        output.sum().backward()
+        assert hidden_states.grad is not None
+        assert hidden_states.grad.shape == hidden_states.shape
+
+    def test_forward_backward_with_mhc_recompute(self):
+        hidden_size, n, s, b = 64, 4, 8, 2
+        layer = self._make_layer(
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            num_streams=n,
+            recompute_granularity="selective",
+            recompute_modules=["core_attn", "mhc"],
+        )
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(s, b, n * hidden_size, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+        attention_mask = torch.ones((1, 1, s, s), dtype=bool, device="cuda")
+
+        manager = MHCCheckpointManager()
+        manager.is_last_layer_in_recompute_block = True
+        output, _ = layer(
+            hidden_states=hidden_states,
+            attention_mask=attention_mask,
+            mhc_recompute_manager=manager,
+        )
+
+        assert output.shape == (s, b, n * hidden_size)
+        manager.discard_all_outputs_and_register_unified_recompute(output)
+        output.sum().backward()
+        assert hidden_states.grad is not None

**[SUGGESTION Style]** This branch makes the comment above it wrong.

**What's wrong:** [L291-L293](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection.py#L291-L293) says the fused path does projection and `compute_h` in one op, so `_projection_and_get_norm` (and therefore `_proj_rms_op`) "is only ever reached on the unfused path". With `enable_identity_hyper_connections=True` and `use_fused_mhc=True`, this line sets `_proj_rms_compute_h_op = None`. `compute_mappings` then takes its `else` branch and calls `_projection_and_get_norm` → `native_proj_rms` even though `use_fused_mhc` is on. Your own `test_use_fused_mhc_keeps_native_projection` runs exactly this path.

**Why it matters:** this comment is the only stated reason `_proj_rms_op` is assigned the native op unconditionally. If someone trusts it and moves `_proj_rms_op` into the non-fused `else` branch, iHC with `use_fused_mhc` breaks.

**Fix:** change only the comment at L291-L293:
```python
        # The fused mHC path computes the projection and compute_h in one op, so
        # _projection_and_get_norm (and therefore _proj_rms_op) is reached on the
        # unfused path and on the iHC path, including iHC with use_fused_mhc.
```

**Keep:** `self._proj_rms_op = native_proj_rms` stays unconditional and unchanged. Both the unfused path and the iHC fused path need it.

**Check:** this only changes a comment. Confirm that `TestIdentityHyperConnectionModule::test_use_fused_mhc_keeps_native_projection` and the existing mHC fused-path tests still pass unchanged.

**[SUGGESTION Style]** `_compute_h` can now return `None` as its third value, but its signature at [L362](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection.py#L362) still says `-> Tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor]`.

**What's wrong:** the docstring was updated to say "or None under iHC", but the annotation was not, so the two disagree.

**Why it matters:** a caller that relies on the annotation could call `.view()` on `h_res` without checking for `None`. That would fail only on the iHC path.

**Fix:** at L362 (`Optional` is already imported at L4):
```python
    def _compute_h(self, proj: Tensor, r: Tensor) -> Tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Optional[Tensor]]:
```

**Keep:** leave `compute_mappings` as `Tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor]`. It always returns a real `h_res`: the Sinkhorn output for mHC and the identity for iHC. Changing an annotation does not affect `@torch.compile` on `_compute_h`.

**Check:** this only changes an annotation. Confirm that `ruff` and `pylint` still pass, and that L362 matches the docstring at L373 and the `return h_pre, h_post, None` here.

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=low -->

Strict review passed — no significant issues found. LGTM

**Findings:** CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, SUGGESTION: 2. Both are documentation fixes in [hyper_connection.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection.py). The iHC change makes two existing statements wrong, and neither fix changes runtime behavior:
- A comment saying when `_proj_rms_op` is used ([L291-L293](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection.py#L291-L293)).
- The return annotation of `_compute_h` ([L362](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/megatron/core/transformer/hyper_connection.py#L362)).

**What I checked and found correct:**
- **iHC parameter layout:** `mapping_proj` and `bias` have `2n` outputs. `alpha_res` is registered as `None`. The `mark_keep_in_fp32` and `sequence_parallel` calls skip it when it is missing. iHC never reads `alpha_res` in the native `_compute_h` or the fused H_post/BDA kernels.
- **`compute_mappings`:** under iHC it builds a contiguous `[s, b, n, n]` identity in the activation dtype that does not require grad, and skips Sinkhorn. The mHC fused and native paths are unchanged; the `h_res.view(s, b, n, n)` call just moved into the Sinkhorn argument.
- **Kernel selection with `use_fused_mhc`:** iHC keeps the fused aggregate and `h_post_bda` kernels. The projection goes through the native `_projection_and_get_norm`, because the fused projection kernel assumes the `n^2 + 2n` layout.
- **`TransformerLayerNode.detach`** ([fine_grained_callables.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/megatron/core/models/gpt/fine_grained_callables.py#L406-L419)): only tensors that require grad are recorded for the backward bridge. `backward_impl` still pairs each recorded tensor with its detached copy, and `ScheduleNode._backward` accepts a variable number of gradients. Every bridged mHC tensor requires grad, so mHC behavior is unchanged.
- **Config:** `enable_identity_hyper_connections` defaults to `False`. Setting it without `enable_hyper_connections` raises an error. `ArgumentGroupFactory` generates the CLI flag automatically, and the flag is registered in the hybrid-MoE `GOLDEN_CONFIG`. Every new identifier is actually used.
- **Test helper teardown** ([test_utilities.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/tests/unit_tests/test_utilities.py#L115-L140)):
  - It copies `ps._global_process_group_list`, which holds only the groups this rank joined through MCore's `create_group`.
  - It resets the FP8 and DTensor caches, calls `ps.destroy_model_parallel()`, then destroys the remaining groups in reverse creation order.
  - WORLD is preserved, and so are the `HyperCommGrid` groups, which are created with `new_subgroups_by_enumeration`.
- **Other users of the changed shapes:** I found no other code that depends on the `alpha_res` or `mapping_proj` shapes. [gpt_hybrid_conversion.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/tools/checkpoint/gpt_hybrid_conversion.py) has no hyper-connection handling. The hybrid wrapper ([hybrid_block.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py)) only passes `h_res` through.

The PR says the identity is materialized and run through a bmm on purpose, with kernel shortcuts for the identity case planned as a follow-up. I treated that as an intentional design decision and did not flag it.

**Overall risk:** low.
- The feature is opt-in and off by default.
- The mHC numerics and schedule paths are unchanged.
- The wider change to how the test harness cleans up process groups has its own regression tests in [test_process_group_cleanup.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/5cf1a2003591696b4b68330e0188c517f1659662/tests/unit_tests/test_process_group_cleanup.py).

> **Note:** formal approval is not available for this request, so this review is posted as a comment only.
